clue.text: Third attempt to hold it back in time

indicators.note: to hold something is to grip it inside, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: an attempt is a try

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so these letters are read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A third try at holding back the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: the reversed pronoun goes inside the period of time first, and only then does the attempt wrap the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Tertiary is the ordinal-style adjective for third in rank or order, as in tertiary education or the Tertiary geological period.

clue.text: Hot video allowed to circulate? I know what you're thinking

definitions.note: a remark that characterises the answer rather than a noun synonym

indicators.note: circulating means coming back round, so the string runs the opposite way

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
a video is a tape
allowed means let

explanation.surface: Someone shares a racy video and a knowing friend says they can guess what you are thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: H, TAPE and LET run together, then the whole string is read backwards. The definition is a phrase a mind reader might say, defining by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A mind reader claims to perceive thoughts directly, so saying they know your thoughts is the signature line of such a person.

clue.text: Regretting line omitted from decree

indicators.note: something omitted is left out, so a letter is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: a decree is a ruling
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a line cut from an official decree.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L out of RULING and the remaining letters close up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to feel sorry about something, so the present participle matches the -ing form of regret exactly.

clue.text: Impossible illusion? Prank with no credit, I repeatedly fancy

indicators.note: to fancy is to imagine or embellish, so the letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the letter I used twice, as repeatedly asks

explanation.surface: A practical joke that earns no credit; someone keeps imagining an impossible illusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is all of PRANK, NO CREDIT and two I's; the question mark ends the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian rope trick is a legendary conjuring feat, a rope rising unsupported for a boy to climb, long believed never actually performed.

clue.text: Bit of sausage outrageous in place of carnival dish

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so these letters go within another word

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is famous for its carnival

indicators.note: a bit of something is a small piece of it, here just its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of sausage
OTT, over the top, means outrageous

explanation.surface: A scandalous chunk of sausage turns up in a festival dish.
explanation.walkthrough: S and OTT together go inside RIO. OTT stands for over the top, a common British shorthand for excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice preparation cooked in stock, so it is one example of a plated meal.

clue.text: Backing for lawyers probing US spies regarding much of Middle East?

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the assembled letters are read right to left
a probe pushes inside something, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
the Bar is the legal profession of barristers

explanation.surface: Lawyers investigating American spies over Middle Eastern matters need backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing for' governs everything after it, so the reversal comes last, after the lawyers are inside the spies. The definition is adjectival, describing the region's language and culture.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic describes the language and culture shared across most countries in that region, so it applies to much of it.

clue.text: New student blocking access for training

indicators.note: to block a passage is to sit in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: recourse is access to a source of help
a fresher is a first-year university student in Britain

explanation.surface: A new student stands in the way of entry to a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: A fresher is the British word for a first-year university student; it splits the word for access after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher course is a short programme of instruction updating someone's skills, so it is a form of training.

clue.text: Setback for bridge support, losing a tool

indicators.note: to lose something is to be without it, so a letter drops out

parts.note: a blow is a setback
for and to are interchangeable in phrases such as a ticket for or to London
an arch holds up a bridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bridge's support gives way and a tool goes missing, a setback for the builders.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOW and TO are followed by ARCH with its A dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowtorch is a handheld burner producing a hot flame for stripping paint or soldering, so it counts as a tool.

clue.text: Cook eggs, divine in cabbage

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: cole is an old name for cabbage, as in coleslaw
DD is Doctor of Divinity, so a divine, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A recipe: cook some eggs and a holy something inside cabbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective praising the dish; it is a noun for a cleric, abbreviated DD.
explanation.definitionFit: Coddled eggs are cooked gently in water just below boiling, so the verb names exactly that method of egg preparation.

clue.text: Second year in pub about to become harmonious

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so these letters go within another word

parts.note: an inn is a pub
S is the abbreviation for second
Y is the abbreviation for year
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A second-year student in the pub is about to get on well with everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: S and Y sit inside INN, then C follows; 'about to' tempts as a single phrase, but 'about' is C and 'to become' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Things working in sync are synchronised, moving together in agreement, which matches being harmonious.

clue.text: Face the other way to receive King and Northern nobleman

indicators.note: going the other way means facing backwards, so the letters are read right to left
to receive something is to take it in, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: a dial is a clock face
R is Rex, king

explanation.surface: Someone turns away to welcome a king and a nobleman from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face the other way' reads as one instruction to turn round, but 'Face' is the noun DIAL, reversed to LAID before taking R.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish landowner of standing, and Scotland is the north of Britain, hence a nobleman of the north.

clue.text: Celebrated female staff about one display of aplomb

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it in song
F is the abbreviation for female
a staff is a rod
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Famous women employees around an individual show great composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celebrated female staff' reads as famous women workers; 'Celebrated' is the verb SANG and 'staff' a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Sang-froid, French for cold blood, is calm composure under pressure, the quality on show when someone acts with aplomb.

clue.text: Display time in food store

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pantry is a store for food
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A sign showing the time inside a grocery shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Display time' reads like a shop clock, but 'Display' is the definition and 'time' is the piece that goes inside the store.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageantry is elaborate ceremonial show, spectacle put on for an audience, so it is a grand public display.

clue.text: Praise being without work? Not I

indicators.note: saying not to a letter means it is refused entry, so that letter drops out

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
toil is hard work

explanation.surface: Is it worth praising a life without work? Someone answers: not me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Praise being' tempts as a phrase about worship, but 'being' only links; EX is followed by TOIL with its I removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud something enthusiastically, a verb synonym of praise used in the same transitive way.

clue.text: Globe hosting The Ring? On the contrary, it offers Baroque music

definitions.note: describes the instrument rather than naming it

indicators.note: a host takes a guest inside; 'On the contrary' swaps host and guest round
says the opposite holds, so the guest becomes the host and the other piece goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
an orb is a globe
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: The Globe theatre staging Wagner's Ring cycle, but the music turns out to be Baroque.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, ORB would hold THE O; 'On the contrary' reverses the roles, so THE plus O hold ORB. The Globe is Shakespeare's London theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorbo is a large long-necked lute widely played in seventeenth-century continuo, so it is an instrument producing Baroque sounds.

clue.text: Large gem carrying bit of sparkle for a bishop

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: epic means on a large scale

indicators.note: a bit of something is a small piece of it, here just its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of sparkle
an opal is a gem

explanation.surface: A big sparkly gem fit for a bishop's ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large gem' reads as one item, but the two words supply separate pieces, with the sparkle's first letter tucked into the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopal is the adjective relating to bishops, from Greek episkopos, overseer, so it means of or for such a churchman.

clue.text: Firm very popular round Republican group

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: something hot is in great demand
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A popular company surrounding a Republican faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective meaning solid; it is a noun for a company, abbreviated as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort is a band of people with something in common, originally a Roman military unit, so it is a group.

clue.text: Increased power around river nearer the mountains

parts.note: prices that are up have increased

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: steam is motive power
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Greater power around a river closer to the hills, perhaps a hydroelectric plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power' here is the old motive force of engines and locomotives, not electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivers rise in high ground and flow down, so travelling against the current takes you toward their sources in the hills.

clue.text: Clingy type, exhausted, and from France

parts.note: limp means drained of energy
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A worn-out, needy hanger-on from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from France' tells you to give 'and' in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a shellfish that sticks fast to rocks, and figuratively a person who will not let go of others.

clue.text: Corporation accepting a lot of change in the boring stuff

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a corporation is a jocular word for a pot belly, a tum

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to edit is to change

explanation.surface: A company takes in a lot of change and the work gets dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' wants to be a business; it is the old jokey word for a large stomach, which then swallows most of the change.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is monotony and dullness, so it is a noun for whatever is tiresome and uninteresting.

clue.text: Church activity declining, mostly trendy

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: something declining is getting worse
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: Churchgoing is falling off, though what remains is mostly fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' looks like it qualifies 'trendy', but it trims the declining word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship is the act of honouring God in services and prayer, the central thing a congregation does.

clue.text: Our group back film?

parts.note: we is the pronoun for our group
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Our team agrees to put money into a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the verb to fund, or a reversal signal; it is the rear of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Western is a cowboy movie genre set in the American frontier, so it is one kind of motion picture.

clue.text: Pacific holiday spot? Almost worth following second person from Paris

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the final letter is cut
following means coming after, so the earlier-named piece is placed later in the answer

parts.note: tu is the French for you, the second person
worth is value

explanation.surface: A Parisian finds a Pacific resort nearly worth the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The French 'you' comes first because 'following' sends the worth piece after it. The question mark flags that a whole nation is being called a holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuvalu is a small island country in the South Pacific, so it is a place someone might visit there, loosely a vacation destination.

clue.text: Article from Le Monde, astute in dismissing English as a whole

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: cute can mean sharp or shrewd
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A sharp piece in Le Monde that leaves out the English entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Monde is a French newspaper, so the article is French. CUTE in its older sense of shrewd loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncut is complete, not abridged or shortened, like a film released in full, so it is entire.

clue.text: Unsettle dance venue ready to rake in millions

indicators.note: raking something in means gathering it inside, so one letter goes within

parts.note: a disco is a dance club
fit means ready, as in fit for duty
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A nightclub poised to make a fortune upsets someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake in millions' sounds like profit, but it just places the abbreviation for million inside the joined venue and readiness words.
explanation.definitionFit: To discomfit someone is to make them uneasy or disconcerted, a transitive verb meaning much the same as unsettle.

clue.text: Entertainment area including a collection of animals

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: fun is entertainment
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: An entertainment zone with a menagerie, like a safari park.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside FUN, then A for area follows; the clue gives area before 'a' but the pieces assemble the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauna is the whole set of animal life in a region or period, so it is a gathering of creatures.

clue.text: Quantity of current illuminated Cornish resort, but not foremost expanse

indicators.note: leaving out what is foremost means the opening letter goes

parts.note: an amp is a unit of electric current
lit means illuminated
Bude is a seaside resort town in Cornwall, England

explanation.surface: Electricity lighting up a Cornish seaside town, though not its main stretch of beach.
explanation.walkthrough: AMP and LIT are followed by BUDE without its first letter. Cornwall is England's south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Amplitude means breadth or spaciousness as well as wave size, so a broad extent of space is one of its senses.

clue.text: Most of beaten path

indicators.note: most of something is all but a little, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a routed army has been soundly beaten

explanation.surface: Much of a well-trodden track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten path' reads as one stock phrase; 'beaten' is ROUTED, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is the way taken to get from one place to another, so it is a path or course.

clue.text: You texted knight story about King? It's not the same

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: U is text-speak for you
N is the chess notation for knight
a story can be a lie
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: Someone texts a story about a king to a knight and notices it doesn't add up.
explanation.walkthrough: U and N lead, then LIE wraps K.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlike means dissimilar or different in nature, an adjective that matches a description of things that differ.

clue.text: Description of some deliveries supervised by a route manager, primarily

parts.note: working under someone means being supervised by them
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only opening letters are kept

parts.note: first letters of route and manager

explanation.surface: Parcel deliveries overseen by the person who plans the van's rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' suggests parcels, but in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An underarm ball is bowled with the hand below shoulder level, a style of bowling, so the word describes certain balls in cricket.
